label: Official TimeFuse router adapted to the BasicTS controlled protocol. This is NOT a reproduction of the TimeFuse paper's published benchmark numbers -- it reuses TimeFuse's official routing mechanism (meta-features + ModelFusor architecture + training procedure) inside this project's existing frozen-expert / router_train / router_val protocol, on datasets and expert pools the TimeFuse paper did not use in this configuration.
modification_required_for_integration: meta_feature.py's extract_meta_feature() calls statsmodels adfuller() and AutoReg(...).fit() per variable, which raise on a channel that is exactly constant within the current window (a real occurrence in BasicTS data, e.g. ExchangeRate/BeijingAirQuality/Traffic flat stretches) -- the official function has no handling for this and crashes. A wrapper extract_meta_feature_robust() (experiments/behavioral_competence/timefuse_probe/meta_feature_cache.py) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the official formula, adding ONLY a try/except around the two statsmodels calls that substitutes NaN on failure -- verified numerically identical to the official function on every window where no exception occurs (see meta_feature_cache.py docstring). The resulting NaN is handled by the SAME nan_to_num(nan=0.0) convention the official Dataset_Meta.__init__ already applies to any NaN in x_meta.

The official notebook trains ONE ModelFusor JOINTLY across multiple datasets simultaneously (length-aligned loaders over meta_train_data_names). This experiment instead trains ONE ModelFusor PER DATASET, independently, to match the single-dataset controlled protocol used by every other method (Simplex, LearnedProbe, C-Rank, etc.) in this experiment family. All per-dataset hyperparameters (architecture, loss, optimizer, schedule, epochs, batch size, seed) are otherwise unchanged from the official per-batch training step.

Official y_model_preds has shape [B,K,H,F] (expert axis at dim=1, TSLib convention); this codebase's forecasts_all has shape [N,H,F,K] (expert axis last, BasicTS/walk-forward cache convention). Weight-broadcasting is adapted accordingly (weights.view(B,1,1,K) instead of weights.unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1)) -- a pure indexing/shape adaptation, not a methodological change.

Official training loss is computed over the full unmasked [B,H,F] tensor (nn.SmoothL1Loss default reduction='mean'). This experiment applies BasicTS's existing target_masks convention (all-True for these four datasets, confirmed no missing values) before averaging, for consistency with every other method in this project; a no-op in practice here but included for correctness if any dataset had missing values.

Process-level parallelism (concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor) is used to compute meta-features across independent windows -- required because Traffic (862 raw channels) takes ~3.15s/window serially (~9h for its ~10k windows) with the official per-variable statsmodels calls; parallelization does not change any feature value (verified: each window's feature vector is independent of every other window's, and results are concatenated back in original order).

official_files_used.README.md: inspected for architecture description confirming 'observed history -> passive meta-features -> ModelFusor -> softmax weights -> weighted forecast'.
official_files_used.meta_feature.py: extract_meta_feature() / batch_extract_meta_features() used verbatim, unmodified. 22-dim passive meta-feature vector per window: mean, std, min, max, skewness, kurtosis, autocorrelation_mean, stationarity (ADF test), rate_of_change_mean/std, autoreg_coef_mean, residual_std_mean, frequency_mean/peak, spectral_entropy/variation/skewness/kurtosis, covariance_mean/max/min/std.
official_files_used.run_config.json: inspected for reference (datasets/models/forecast_settings used in the official paper benchmark); not used directly since this experiment runs its own controlled BasicTS protocol.
official_files_used.run_timefuse_exp.ipynb: Cell '[4] TimeFuse: Fusor training and evaluation' inspected for the exact official ModelFusor training procedure: Adam optimizer lr=0.0005, StepLR(step_size=10, gamma=0.1), criterion=nn.SmoothL1Loss(beta=0.01), n_epochs=5, batch_size=64, random_seed=2021 (random.seed/torch.manual_seed/np.random.seed), dim_meta_feats=22. These exact hyperparameters are reused unmodified in this experiment's train_timefuse_fusor().
official_files_used.timefuse.py: ModelFusor class used verbatim, unmodified: nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim) with kaiming_uniform_ init, forward = softmax(fc(x), dim=-1). TorchScaler/get_scaler('standard') (sklearn StandardScaler wrapper) used verbatim for feature scaling.
